classification.difficultyReason: Combines a central angle, supplementary cyclic angles and a triangle angle sum.

content.prompt: Given $\angle CBD=10^\circ$ and $\angle BOD=100^\circ$, find $\angle BDC$.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral A–B–C–D with A left, B upper right, C right and D lower right. Centre O has radii OB and OD. Numerical givens remain in the stem.
spec.mathematics: The minor central angle BOD spans the arc through C; A lies on the other arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source point labels and edges appear.

answer.short:
$40^\circ$

Use the central angle to find $\angle BAD$, then supplementary angles and the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference subtending the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAD&=\tfrac12\times100^\circ\\\angle BAD&=50^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BCD&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\\angle BCD&=130^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of $\triangle BCD$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BDC&=180^\circ-130^\circ-10^\circ\\\angle BDC&=40^\circ.\end{align*}$$
